name: Tenancy
purpose: Resolves which organization a request belongs to, and keeps every other tenant's rows unreachable. The layer every other module sits on.
features: Host header → organization lookup, Redis-cached with negative caching for unknown hosts
`withTenant(ctx, …)` / `forTenant(ctx)` set transaction-local Postgres session vars, so a pooled connection cannot leak context between requests
`setTenantContext()` adopts an organization mid-transaction, for registration only
`withUserIdentity()` reads only the caller's own `memberships` rows, pre-tenant
`assertRlsActive()` refuses to boot the app on an owner (RLS-bypassing) connection
Self-serve registration: organization + domain + first branch + owner + membership + ORG_OWNER grant + trial subscription in one transaction
userActions: Register a clinic from the apex domain (4-step signup with live slug availability)
Be provisioned by a platform admin, optionally converting a demo request
limitations: Custom domains are modelled (`organization_domains.isPlatformSub`) but there is no verification flow
`organizations` and `organization_domains` are deliberately outside RLS — the host→tenant lookup cannot require the context it establishes
Slug availability is a customer-list oracle by construction; mitigated only by rate limiting

name: Authentication
purpose: Proves who a caller is and issues the session they act under. Password and phone-OTP, refresh rotation with reuse detection.
features: Password login by email or phone, constant-time failure, one message for every cause including 'not a member here'
Phone OTP: hashed at rest, single-use, attempt-capped
Access token is a 15-minute stateless JWT; refresh token is an opaque 256-bit string stored only as a SHA-256 hash
Refresh rotation — replaying a rotated token revokes the whole family
Account lockout after 5 failed attempts
Branch and organization switching without re-authenticating
Sessions in httpOnly host-only cookies; Next is the BFF, tokens never reach client JS
userActions: Sign in with a password or a one-time code
Switch active branch or organization
Sign out
limitations: OTP delivery is a logging stub behind `services/notification/sender.ts`, pending TRAI DLT registration
`emailVerifiedAt` is never set — there is no email verification flow
`user_identities` exists for SSO but no provider is wired

name: IAM
purpose: Who may do what, where. Roles cloned from the system set, granted per branch or clinic-wide, with per-person exceptions.
features: Resolution order DENY > GRANT > role grants, branch-scoped, with validity windows
A NULL `branch_id` on a `membership_roles` row means every branch in the organization
Custom roles are clones of read-only system roles; a database trigger stops a tenant shadowing a system role code
Per-person GRANT/DENY overrides on top of role defaults
Member suspension and restoration
Three privilege-escalation guards in `services/iam/guards.ts` (STATUS.md says four; the file header says three)
userActions: Create a custom role by cloning a system role
Grant or take away a role, for one branch or all
Add or clear a per-person permission exception
Suspend or restore a colleague
limitations: The escalation guards are application-level only — the database does not enforce them, and two of them cannot be, because the database has no idea what its caller is allowed to do. A direct SQL write bypasses them
Resolved access is cached in Redis; every write must call `invalidateUserAccess` or a revoked role keeps working until the TTL

name: Branches
purpose: The places a clinic operates from. One organization, one or many branches — a solo clinic and a hospital group are the same shape.
features: Branch CRUD with a tenant-qualified `code`
Weekly operating hours with per-day slot minutes
Closure dates
Soft delete via `deletedAt`, never a boolean
userActions: Open a branch
Edit branch details and GST number
Set the opening-hours week strip
Retire a branch
limitations: Closures are modelled but no screen manages them
`branch_operating_hours` and `branch_closures` have no `organization_id`; they are protected by a parent-scoped RLS policy through `branches`

name: Invitations
purpose: How a colleague gets into a clinic. Issue, revoke, resend, and an unauthenticated accept page.
features: Token hashed at rest, same treatment as a refresh token
Invitation carries the role and the branches it will grant
Revoke and resend
Unauthenticated `/join` page that creates the user, membership and role grant on accept
userActions: Invite someone by email or phone, choosing role and branches
Revoke or resend a pending invitation
Accept an invitation and set a password
limitations: Delivery is the same logging stub as OTP — the invitation link is only visible in the API logs
No expiry sweep; expired invitations are filtered at read time, never deleted

name: Patients
purpose: The people being treated. The first PHI in the product: identity is org-wide so a duplicate can be found before it is created, attendance is branch-local, and every read is recorded in `data_access_logs`.
features: Registration issuing an org-wide UHID and a branch-local MRN through `issueNumber`, gapless and concurrency-safe
Duplicate detection on phone, ABHA, national id, and name+date-of-birth together — org-wide, across branches the caller cannot see
Trigram search over name and phone, plus exact UHID and MRN, scoped to the caller's branches or widened to the organization
Allergies, problems and medicines behind a separate `patient.medical_history.*` permission
Address and next of kin, with a guardian flag distinct from the emergency contact
Age recorded as a birth date OR a stated approximation, never both
userActions: Search for a patient by name, phone or number
Register a new patient at a clinic
Register an existing patient at a second clinic
Open a patient record and read the chart
Record and withdraw an allergy, a problem or a medicine
Stop a medicine
limitations: ⚠️ `patients` carries NO `branch_isolation` policy, deliberately — the branch boundary is on `patient_registrations`. See ADR-0016 before 'fixing' it
`patient_allergies.medicine_id` and `patient_conditions.diagnosis_id` are absent until the Phase 5 catalogues exist; both carry free text instead
No merge flow yet. `status = MERGED` and `merged_into_id` exist, tied together by a CHECK, and nothing writes them
Family history, insurances, documents and consents from the §6 ERD are not built
`patients.status = DECEASED` and `deceased_on` are storable but no screen sets them

name: Appointments
purpose: Booking, and the availability engine behind it. PHI: a patient, a doctor and a reason disclose more together than any one of them. Unlike `patients`, `appointments` IS branch-scoped — identity follows the person, attendance belongs to the clinic it happened at.
features: One availability engine every booking path goes through — recurring blocks, APPROVED exceptions, EXTRA_SHIFT, branch closures, past slots and the advisory per-block cap
Slot length resolved through the single chain of ADR-0015; the engine imports `effectiveSlotMinutes` rather than re-deriving it
Every wall-clock to instant conversion done in Postgres with an explicit `::timestamp` cast, never in Node
Double-booking refused by a GiST EXCLUDE constraint whose predicate excludes CANCELLED and NO_SHOW, so cancelling frees the slot with no release step
A transition map in the service and CHECK constraints in the database; NO_SHOW is unreachable after a check-in
Branch-local appointment numbers from `issueNumber`, issued immediately before the insert so the counter lock is one statement wide
Booking registers the patient at the branch on their first visit there, reusing the MRN issue
An append-only status trail, by the same owner-exempt trigger plus REVOKE as `audit_logs`
userActions: See which slots are free for a doctor on a day
Book an appointment against a free slot
Move a booking to another time or another doctor
Check a patient in, start the consultation, mark it seen
Cancel a booking with a stated reason
Record that a patient did not attend
Read one booking and its status trail
limitations: ⚠️ `appointment_status_history` RESTATES the branch predicate from `appointments`. RLS is NOT applied inside a policy expression's subquery, so it cannot be inherited — change one and change the other
The engine cannot see a booking for the same doctor at a branch outside the caller's scope, and must not. The EXCLUDE constraint catches it and the 409 never names who holds the slot
`maxPatients` is advisory — two concurrent bookings into different free slots can take a block one over its cap
A reschedule writes no status-history row; the move is in `audit_logs` only
No queue tokens, no walk-in flow — Stage 5. `QUEUE_TOKEN` numbering exists and nothing writes it
Nothing sends a reminder; `appointment.reminder_hours_before` is seeded and no worker reads it
The day board deliberately writes no `data_access_logs` row — see the service header before adding one

name: Audit
purpose: An append-only record of who changed what. Ids and permission codes only — never a name, never PHI.
features: Structured before/after diff of the changed fields
Actor, organization, branch, action and target on every row
Written inside the same transaction as the change it records
limitations: No viewer — rows are only readable via SQL
`data_access_logs` for PHI reads is planned but does not exist
Nothing enforces append-only at the database level; it is a convention

name: PlatformConsole
purpose: What the platform operator sees. Demo-request pipeline, provisioning, and eventually impersonation.
features: Demo-request list with status pipeline
Provision an organization from a demo request or from scratch
Platform admin login, separate from any tenant
userActions: Review incoming demo requests
Provision a clinic
Sign in to the platform console at the `admin.` subdomain
limitations: Impersonation is not implemented. The session it mints must carry a real branch scope — a platform admin has no membership, so `loadUserAccess` returns null and every branch-scoped write would be refused
No plan or subscription management screens

name: Marketing
purpose: The apex domain. Landing page, signup, legal pages and the demo form — everything that happens before a tenant exists.
features: Landing page: hero, six-station journey rail, modules, multi-branch, isolation, India-first, pricing, demo form
The design system every later screen inherits — surgical-green palette, IBM Plex, spacing and radius scale, in `apps/web/src/app/globals.css`
4-step signup with live slug availability checking
Demo form: rate-limited, honeypot plus timing check, silent discard, deduplicated
Measured accessibility pass — 4.5:1 contrast, 24×24 targets, skip link, rail pause control, `aria-describedby` on every field
userActions: Read about the product
Book a demo
Register a clinic
Read the privacy policy, terms and DPA
limitations: Legal pages are unreviewed drafts with ~30 unfilled placeholders and a visible 'not yet in force' banner
`src/lib/analytics.ts` is a no-op seam pending a DPDP consent decision
No real OG image; footer brand facts are placeholders
Screen-reader behaviour in a real AT and the OS reduced-motion toggle are implemented but never exercised end to end

name: Notifications
purpose: The seam every outbound message goes through. Real logic, no delivery.
features: One `sender.ts` seam for OTP codes and invitation links
Logs the message instead of sending it
limitations: Nothing is delivered. Blocked on TRAI DLT registration for SMS and Meta template approval for WhatsApp
No notification templates table, no provider abstraction, no delivery-status tracking

name: Worker
purpose: Background jobs on BullMQ. Every queue is registered; only stubs process them.
features: Redis connection and queue registration
limitations: No processors exist — queues accept jobs that nothing consumes
No scheduled jobs, no dead-letter handling, no metrics rollup

name: Contracts
purpose: Zod schemas shared by API and web. The request/response shape is written once and both sides import it.
features: Validation and inferred TypeScript types from the same declaration
Grouped by domain: common, auth, tenancy, marketing
limitations: No runtime response validation on the web side — contracts type the response but nothing parses it
Chosen over tRPC/ts-rest deliberately; revisit if a mobile client appears
